title: Coco Labs Launches First AI for Editable Layered Design Files
summary:
A startup founded by former engineers from Google Brain and DeepMind has released a generative tool that converts website branding into multi-layered assets. The new model, Vyb, extracts logos, hex colors, and fonts from a brand's website to create marketing graphics as structured elements rather than flat pixels. Because text remains as live strings and graphics as vectors, the resulting designs can be exported to Figma as fully editable files without regenerating the entire image.

In tests involving 145 Google fonts, Vyb achieved a 90.3% pixel overlap score against programmatic renders, compared to 76.0% for the strongest image model in the study. Another internal test showed the model matched requested font shapes 95.3% of the time. CEO @anurahk and CTO @DavidZats spent two years building Vyb in stealth to move AI design away from generic output and toward professional workflows.

selectedTweets.text:
Design is the next place where models are learning to output structure instead of pixels.

Vyb, a design model from Coco Labs, builds a graphic element by element, each on its own layer, so text stays live text, graphics stay vectors and photos stay pixels.

That changes what you get back. The headline can be retyped. The logo is the logo file, pulled from your website along with your fonts and exact colors.

Across 145 randomly chosen Google fonts, scored by pixel overlap (IoU) against a programmatic render, Vyb reached 90.3%. The measurement ceiling on that test is 94.4%, and the strongest image model in the comparison reached 76.0%.

Because every layer keeps its native type, the export to Figma carries the structure across intact.
